macro.story:
The facts first. SPY sits at 747.41, above its 50- and 200-day moving averages but down roughly 1% on the week with MACD below its signal line and RSI a middling 52.0 — a slow bleed inside an uptrend. QQQ (705.35) has quietly dropped below its 50-day and is off 4.4% over 21 days, with RSI 46.7 and MACD firmly negative — tech is the weak link. VIX is at 18.21, up nearly 9% in 5 days, VIX3M/VIX ratio has compressed 11% (still in contango), 10Y yield sits at 4.66% (up 2.5% in 5d), and the DXY has firmed to 101.3. Commodities are split: WTI crude has ripped +15% in 5d and +24% in 21d to $90.88 with RSI 69.6 (overbought and extended), while gold and silver are down 1.6% and 2.3% respectively on the day as the dollar strengthens — the validated inverse DXY-metals relationship at work.

The prevailing sentiment leans firmly bullish, but the substance of the tracked conversation is telling: the dominant narrative is AI capex — Alphabet's blowout print, AMD's $5B Anthropic deal, hyperscaler spending, and compute constraints — with heavy chatter around GOOGL, NVDA, TSM, MU, INTC, NBIS, and crypto/miner names like CIFR and IREN. Yet the tape shows QQQ and Technology as the weakest sectors on the board. This is a meaningful conflict: sentiment is anchored on the AI trade while price is quietly rotating out of it. Separately, prominent chart reads in the pulse flag oil ripping through $90–$100 as the actual price story, which is consistent with the sector data. The tracked conversation is not offering a clean attribution for the tech softness or the VIX uptick — treat that gap as real; do not manufacture one.

Sector rotation confirms the split: Energy is HOT (score 9.8, RSI 67.7, MACD bullish), Real Estate HOT, Financials and Utilities QUALIFYING, while Technology, Nasdaq 100, Communication Services, and Consumer Discretionary are the laggards. The Early-Runway rotation signal — a validated edge — is lit for Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (rotation score 0.97, still early in its run at ~50% through a typical spell), Diagnostics & Research, Staffing & Employment Services, and REIT-Industrial. That is where a long-only trader should be hunting.

Forward watch: (1) whether WTI holds above $88 support or reverses — an oil failure would remove the strongest tailwind on the board; (2) whether QQQ can reclaim its 50-day or lose $702 support, which would either heal or extend the tech drag; (3) VIX behavior around 18–19 — a break above 20 would cap confidence further; (4) DXY 101 breakout — continued dollar strength keeps metals under pressure.

**[THE SPINE]** The energy-and-rates squeeze is the dominant force this week. WTI is up 24.4% over 21 days with RSI at 69.8 and pushing the upper Bollinger band, and the entire yield curve is bleeding higher — 2Y RSI 66.6, 5Y RSI 67.5, 10Y RSI 68.1, all above their upper bands or pressing them. That combination — sticky energy plus a re-steepening in rising yields — is what the tape is being organized around, not AI, not the dollar. Everything else this week is a second derivative of that.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** Regime prints CHOPPY with 6/10 confidence and breadth is soft (bullish 21.5% vs bearish 50.9% on 5d), so this is not a clean risk-on tape supporting the spine — it's a rotation tape. VIX at 18.6 with the term structure in contango keeps a lid on outright panic, but the 24h VIX pop of 13.8% says hedging is being re-engaged as yields extend. The DXY_METALS_TAG signal is ACTIVE — DXY above both 21d and 50d SMA — and that's a durable headwind for Gold (-1.6% 21d, RSI 45), Silver (-6.3%, RSI 42), and by extension the precious metals theme, which is already flagged FADING. On WTI, TLT, and the 10Y: the backtest is explicit — no mean-reversion edge, so treat oil as trending up and long bonds/yields as trending against duration, not as stretched rubber bands.

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** XLE leads at +10.1% over 21d and +6.1% vs its 50SMA — that is the spine expressed cleanly. XLV (+5.2%) and XLF (+3.2%) round out the leadership, with Financials benefiting from the steeper curve.
